newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealanders equally split on coalition question.
newsitem.headline: New Zealanders equally split on coalition question.

text.p: Voters were almost equally divided as to whether New Zealand First should form a coalition with either the National or Labour parties, according to a TV3-Waikato opinion released on Wednesday.

The poll of 600 people over Monday and Tuesday showed 48.4 percent wanted NZ First to form a coalition with National while 46.2 percent preferred a Labour-NZ First tie-up, well within the poll's 4.0 percent margin of error.

In the preferred prime minister stakes, the poll was also divided, with 40.6 percent opting for Prime Minister Jim Bolger, 39.7 percent for Labour's Helen Clark and just 11 percent for NZ First's Winston Peters.
